title: quota enforcer split-brain due to auth-cache evictions causing intermittent 429 spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a sustained traffic burst across multiple regions, the quota enforcer entered a split-brain state where different gateway nodes held inconsistent auth/usage windows. This resulted in intermittent 429 storms for legitimate traffic and misattribution of quota usage to incorrect tokens. The incident surfaced as an uptick in user 429s, elevated latency for affected routes, and customer support tickets from enterprise customers on Dedicated plans.
impact_summary: ~15 minutes of elevated 429 responses for ~2% of requests globally, affecting several high-throughput customers on Dedicated and Hosted tiers. Estimated revenue impact: low-to-medium for the window, but increased support and trust cost. No data exfiltration or security policy violations observed.

root_cause: A race condition between the quota enforcer's cache eviction path and the auth token lease renewal produced inconsistent in-memory state on a subset of gateway nodes. Specifically: (1) a recent change to eviction heuristics reduced the TTL for hot-key entries under memory pressure, (2) during bursty traffic the auth-lease refresh RPCs were occasionally delayed by transient networking jitter, and (3) an opportunistic optimization that allowed 'optimistic charge' writes without durable coordination produced divergent counters. The combination led to some nodes serving requests without the most recent usage window while others enforced quotas strictly, creating a split-brain that manifested as 429 storms and misattribution.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back the eviction-heuristics change in 2.7.4-canary to the previous stable behavior
Increased auth-lease RPC timeouts and added exponential backoff to reduce renewal failures
Temporarily widened grace threshold to avoid firing hard 429s while we assessed state consistency
long_term_actions: Implement a coordinated leasing protocol for quota windows to eliminate optimistic-only updates (owner: Carlos, due: 2026-03-21)
Add invariant check and automatic heal job that compares node counters to a canonical store and reconciles drift (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-04-04)
Revisit TTL heuristics: introduce adaptive TTL that factors in request heat and node memory pressure, with canary ramp (owner: EngInfra, due: 2026-04-11)
Add sticky routing option for tokens during high churn periods to reduce cross-node lease movement (owner: SRE, due: 2026-04-01)
Expand chaos tests for auth-lease latency and gateway node cache evictions in staging harness (owner: QA, due: 2026-03-28)
Create a post-deployment automated smoke that simulates quota-heavy client patterns and validates no 429 regressions within 15 minutes (owner: Release Eng, due: 2026-03-25)
Document the fallback semantics and update runbook with decision thresholds for widening grace thresholds and safe rollback procedures (owner: Oncall, due: 2026-03-18)
test_plan: Unit tests for eviction/renewal ordering and explicit race scenarios
Integration test: simulate delayed auth-lease RPCs while throughput increases to validate no split-brain occurs
Canary stage: deploy to 5% traffic in us-central with synthetic quota-heavy clients for 24h
Chaos experiment: kill-in-flight auth-lease RPCs and assert reconciliation completes within SLA
rollout_plan: Patch branch with coordinated leasing changes -> internal review -> merge -> deploy to canary (5%) -> monitor 48h -> progressive rollout 5->25->100% with hold windows and automated rollback on 429 rate > 0.5% baseline increase.
monitoring_changes: New metric: quota_counter_drift_per_token (histogram) and alert when drift > 3 for >5m
Dashboard: per-token 429 rate sliced by gateway node to detect early split-brain patterns
SLO check: add canary guard that prevents rollout if synthetic 429 rate above threshold
Log enrichment: include lease_revision and node_id in quota denial logs for fast correlation
